title: Speculative slot reservation with stochastic kernel fallback for continuous batching
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Spiky arrival patterns and heterogeneous sequence lengths lead to tail latency spikes when the admission controller groups requests into batches and the chosen kernel underperforms for a given batch shape. Existing kernel selection heuristics are deterministic and can mispredict for rare but costly shapes during prefill or decode, causing increased 95th/99th percentile latency for latency-sensitive customers.

Proposal: Implement a speculative slot reservation mechanism coupled with a stochastic kernel fallback policy. When a candidate request arrives and the admission controller predicts an ambiguous kernel choice (low confidence), we reserve a lightweight speculative GPU slot and simultaneously probe two execution paths: the predicted optimal kernel and a conservative fallback (smaller, lower-memory, quantized kernel). The scheduler then race-works the first token(s) on both kernels for a short horizon (speculative prefill probe). If the fallback finishes earlier for the initial tokens or the predicted kernel shows early signs of slowdown (higher per-step time), the runtime switches the rest of the decode to the fallback kernel with minimal KV-cache migration. This reduces tail latency by avoiding large rollbacks and expensive re-queuing while preserving throughput for common shapes.

Key ideas: speculative slot reservation (short lived), stochastic decision thresholding (take action when kernel-confidence < X), dual-path probing (optimal + conservative), fast detection signals (early per-token timing, kernel throughput counters), lightweight KV migration strategy, and budgeted speculative resource accounting to avoid capacity exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: 95th and 99th percentile latency for latency-sensitive workloads reduced by >=15% in the perf benchmark compared to baseline admission controller
No more than 5% increase in average GPU cycles per token across mixed workloads after rollout (controlled budget for speculative probes)
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout policy; behavior revertible via console within a minute
End-to-end end-to-end correctness: decoded tokens match deterministic baseline when kernel switch occurs (byte-for-byte or token-for-token depending on model config)
implementation_steps: Instrument kernel prediction path to produce a confidence score and Export early per-token timing metrics to scheduler
Implement speculative_slot_reserver component that can allocate a transient slot with quota accounting
Implement dual-path probe orchestration in admission controller: launch both kernels for N speculative steps
Add lightweight KV migration primitives to move/alias prefix caches between kernels without full copy
Expose rollout flags and budget parameters to console; add observability (per-request tag, speculative_hit/fallback counts)
Benchmark on our perf cluster with mixed-shape trace (short/medium/long) and update staging dashboards
Gradual canary rollout with traffic shaping, monitor tail latency and GPU utilization
risks: Speculative probes could increase GPU contention and raise average cost if budget not enforced
Incorrect kernel switch might cause subtle numerical divergence for some models — requires correctness testing
KV migration latency could negate benefits if not implemented carefully
Complexity in accounting and observability may hide regressions unless instrumented thoroughly
comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Kapoor: Initial spike analysis showed 2–3x latency amplification on rare long-short mixed batches. Proposed speculative fallback as low-risk mitigation compared to requeueing on kernel mismatch.
2026-03-04 Jun Park: Prototype of confidence scoring implemented. Using entropy of shape distribution + historical kernel latency variance. Confidence threshold tuned to 0.28 for staging traffic.
2026-03-06 Infra: Added quota hooks to scheduler; speculative_slot_reserver supports per-tenant budget and global emergency cutoff.
2026-03-07 Performance: Initial microbench indicates speculative probe adds 3% extra cycles on busy clusters but drops 95th latency by 18% for the targeted trace.
2026-03-08 Design review (PM): Concern about customer billing — agreed to mark speculative probes as platform overhead and exclude from customer token billing; update pricing doc after rollout.
2026-03-09 Security review requested by Jun Park: no sensitive data exposed in speculative probes; flagged for final audit (ticket SEC-4421).
2026-03-10 Engineering review: Implemented KV aliasing to avoid copying on switch; validated with GPT2-like model in staging — no correctness diffs within token horizon.
2026-03-11 QA: Added randomized decode fuzzer; found a divergence in mixed-precision path when switching after step 7. Patch pushed to fix quantization state sync (PR #1284).
2026-03-12 Ops: Canary started at 5% for latency-sensitive customers, monitoring per-tenant speculative_hit_rate and GPU probe budget burn. Early signals nominal.
2026-03-13 PM note (Marco Delgado): Prepare rollout announcement and one-pager explaining impact on SLAs, billing, and how customers can opt-out via console flags.
